title: Real lab: lock down a file's permissions
instruction: Real Linux box. A sensitive file at /root/secret.txt is currently readable by everyone, check its mode with `ls -l /root/secret.txt`. Lock it down so ONLY the owner can read and write it (no group, no others). Then click Verify.
setup: printf 'launch codes: 0000\n' > /root/secret.txt; chmod 644 /root/secret.txt; echo '(scenario ready: /root/secret.txt is world-readable)'

verify.command: if [ "$(stat -c '%a' /root/secret.txt 2>/dev/null)" = 600 ]; then echo PERM_OK; else echo PERM_NO mode=$(stat -c '%a' /root/secret.txt 2>/dev/null); fi
verify.success: Solved! 600 means owner read+write and nobody else. chmod's three octal digits are owner/group/other, each a sum of read(4) + write(2) + execute(1).
verify.fail: Not there yet, /root/secret.txt must be mode 600 (owner rw, no access for group or others).
